column1: # Rule heads (C). Each bunsetsu takes, among the candidates on the head chain to its right (so the tree stays
# projective), the first one its most specific matching row accepts; the sentence-final bunsetsu accepts every
# dependent. dep atoms: dt (adn topic pred case adv conj other), kase, link (aux.tsv link names, adn, renyo, final),
# cwc, last, form, comma, nextnoun, pred; ! negates; atoms joined by &. head: noun (the first nominal), pred (the
# first predicate), pred>=X (the first predicate whose clause level is X or wider; an attributive predicate counts as B), next, final.
# level rows: the scope level of a clause link, A < B < C < D (sentence end), after Minami's clause hierarchy.

column5: accompanying action: ながら, たり
sequence, condition, cause by ので, time and purpose
contrast, reason by から, listing し, のに
a case or adverbial phrase depends on the nearest predicate
の-phrases and attributive clauses modify the nearest noun
a topic (は, a noun with a comma) scopes over clauses up to a contrast/reason clause or the end
a conjunction scopes like a topic
a clause depends on the nearest predicate of an equal or wider clause
a B-level clause skips A-level predicates; an attributive clause can hold it
a C-level clause depends on a C-level clause or the end
も marks an argument of the nearest predicate, not a topic
と before a noun phrase joins the two nouns (AとBが)
an interjection belongs to the whole utterance
the adverbial form of an adjective (深く, 静かに) modifies the nearest predicate
a topic set off by a comma scopes over the whole sentence
